Description: Mavia is a queen of the Tanukhids and the spouse of Al-Hawari. With the Tanukhids at war with the eastern Romans, she must weigh the demands of conflict against the cohesion of her followers. Roman commanders may speak the language of protection while seeking service on terms that leave their allies little room to refuse. She listens for the obligation concealed behind a courtesy and asks who can guarantee an envoy's offer. Frontier routes, dependable access to supplies and a voice in religious leadership matter more to her than praise from a distant court. She is ready to defend her people's standing, yet firmness does not require rejecting every settlement. An agreement has value when its safeguards are credible and its burdens can be borne. A leader who accepts separate rewards may weaken the whole confederation; an uncompromising demand for prestige can be just as costly. She therefore measures courage against responsibility, seeking terms that preserve authority without exhausting those who sustain it. Her direct manner expresses pride, but also an awareness that threats are useful only when followers remain willing and able to support them.

Motivations: Preserve Tanukhid cohesion and negotiate service to Rome on terms her followers can sustain.
Protect her people's voice in decisions about frontier obligations and religious leadership.
Values: An alliance must contain reciprocal commitments, not only demands from the stronger partner.
Religious and communal authority cannot be secured by an envoy's unsupported promises.
Fears: Rival leaders accepting separate rewards that leave the confederation divided.
Imperial demands exhausting followers while offering no dependable protection.
